title: Advisory, Training and Influencing the Business
summary: How compliance advises the business on new products, marketing and change, builds compliance awareness through training and earns influence without losing independence.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How compliance advises the business on new products, marketing and change, builds compliance awareness through training and earns influence without losing independence.
Learning Objectives: Provide clear, practical compliance advice on business initiatives and change
Design a training programme that targets the firm's highest compliance risks
Influence senior managers while preserving the function's independence
Syllabus: Advising on new products, marketing materials and business change
Recording advice and managing disagreements with the business
Risk-based training needs analysis and measuring effectiveness
Building a constructive relationship with front-line management
Intended Audience: Heads of compliance, compliance officers and deputies in regulated firms
Compliance analysts and monitoring staff moving into more senior or advisory roles
Risk, legal and business managers who work closely with the compliance function
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of working in or alongside a compliance function in a regulated firm is helpful. No legal qualification is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Compliance and the Compliance Function in Banks (2005)
IOSCO, Compliance Function at Market Intermediaries (2006)
FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
